Personally I have never been a fan of filtering damage into AZ. Now if it is extra target damage then it is a different story. Such as Inferno, hit the main target first and hit AZ with one of the other hits. Even with Coolant Blast there isn't a big reason for it. Sure you filtered 10 damage, getting an extra 2, than doing 11 with Coolant Blast. So 23 damage to someone, great. However Thermal Shockwave would deal 3 targets 2, so 6 cold damage total. Not AZ will take 6 to do another 7 damage. That's 13 damage right there, so Ra did 10 and AZ does 13, that's still 23 damage with AZ taking 4 less damage. It is 4 less damage to a single target, but hitting multiple targets is always a good thing.

Of course you could combine the two, deal AZ the 10 damage that he'll turn into 12. Then on AZ's turn he'll hit 3 for 2, 6 fire to himself, to do 7 cold. That's now 25 damage they dealt out together. That's only an increase in 2 damage, with AZ taking 10 more than before. Plus AZ will now have to start healing, taking away from damage next turn.

Imbued Fire in play changes it though, as now filtering multiple heroes damage makes him rack up more in a single turn, thus using Coolant Blast acutally becomes worth it.

posts.name: Scholars Aide
posts.cooked:
I have read through this article, and taking into account Chris's assertion that these abilities should have some cost, I would like to assert that, in the case of the Pushing The Limits combo for Tachyon, there IS still a cost.

Assuming that you have damage boosted somehow, Tachyon would deal herself 3 damage at the beginning of her turn in order to keep Pushing The Limits around.  If you have Synaptic Interruption in play, it allows you to redirect 3 or more damage that would be dealt to Tachyon to another target, then destroy SI.  I would argue that there IS an inherent cost in that redirection, as using SI to protect yourself from the damage forces you to NOT use it to defend against another threat that may hit you during the environment/villain turns.  So, there is a "cost" to Tachyon keeping PTL around, just not a HP cost.

posts.name: BlueHairedMeerkat

posts.cooked:
BlueHairedMeerkat:

Unless it can be, for example, Smoke Bombed to Mr Fixer with a Driving Mantis. Synaptic Interruption is only one possible way to avoid the damage from Pushing the Limits.

It's damage you're dealing to yourself, not from a villain target so it can't be smoke bombed away, but I agree there are other ways to redirect/not take the damage.

Scholars Aide:

So, there is a "cost" to Tachyon keeping PTL around, just not a HP cost.

Christopher's assertion was that there was meant to be an HP cost, not just "a cost". You could argue that Ra's god combo did have a cost before, that of the time it took to set it up (time is definitely a cost in my book, not just in games) and the fact that relied entirely on ongoings, which are very easy to destroy, and not multiple types that could still be beneficial if only part of it was destroyed, but that's a slippery slope.

And Tachyon's SI is also a benefit at the same time, it does damage to a target you want it to, prevents damage to you and fuels your Lightspeed Barrage all for a single 'action', is the playing of SI and losing it to PtL ultimately a cost or a benefit? Both sides can be argued, very convincingly, and we will never get a definitive answer, because it subjective not objective.

I think for ease of play we stick with what we've got, some HP must be lost to keep the cards around and not re-open this can of worms so soon after the lid has been placed by the designers.
